items.title: Hear live or leave
items.instructions: Use the transcript as a listening script, then answer the question.

payload.transcript: Nora says, ‘I live near the river.’

questions.text: Which word follows I: live or leave?

answers.explanation: The transcript states that Nora lives near the river.

items.title: Clarify one vowel
items.instructions: Respond to a listener who has confused live and leave.

payload.communicative_goal: Clarify that you said live, then restate your personal fact.
payload.expected_output: A brief correction followed by a clear present-simple fact.

rubric.criterion: The response clearly distinguishes live from leave.
The response directly repairs the misunderstanding.

items.title: Construct a repair question
items.instructions: Use every required word to make a clarification question.

payload.scoring_guidance: Accept the exact question with normal capitalization and punctuation.

items.title: Select the intended vowel contrast
items.instructions: Choose the sentence that means the speaker resides nearby.

options.text: I lived near the market tomorrow.

payload.explanation: Live expresses residence; leave does not.

items.title: Write a two-line repair
items.instructions: Write a short exchange that corrects leave to live.

payload.communicative_goal: Write a natural clarification exchange about where someone resides.
payload.expected_output: One question showing the misunderstanding and one correction with a personal fact.

rubric.criterion: Live is used for residence and leave only as the misheard word.
The correction is easy to follow.
